name: Interstitial Lung Disease Specific to Childhood

criteria.description: Persistent respiratory symptoms such as tachypnea, cough, and hypoxemia lasting more than 3 weeks
High-resolution CT scan showing diffuse parenchymal lung abnormalities consistent with interstitial lung disease
Histopathological confirmation of interstitial lung disease when non-invasive tests are inconclusive
Exclusion of infectious, cardiac, immunodeficiency, and environmental causes
Restrictive ventilatory defect and impaired gas exchange on pulmonary function testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent respiratory symptoms >3 weeks plus characteristic HRCT findings and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy is reserved for atypical or unclear cases due to its invasive nature.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoxemia at rest or with exertion
searchTerms: low oxygen levels at rest or exercise
chest wall pulling in during breathing
skin sinking between ribs when breathing hard
mild high blood pressure in lungs

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
Possible autoimmune serologies if associated with connective tissue disease
imaging: High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities, reticular patterns, and cystic changes
Reduced lung volumes on chest X-ray
genetic: Mutations in surfactant protein genes (SFTPC, SFTPB) in familial cases
ABCA3 gene mutations associated with some forms
other: Lung biopsy demonstrating interstitial inflammation, fibrosis, or alveolar proteinosis depending on subtype
Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic genetic mutations in CFTR gene
History of prematurity and neonatal respiratory support
Radiographic evidence of lung injury and fibrosis
Different clinical course and age of onset
Immunoglobulin deficiencies or lymphocyte subset abnormalities

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Development of pulmonary hypertension or cor pulmonale
references: Nathan AM, et al. Childhood Interstitial Lung Disease: A Clinical Review. Pediatr Pulmonol. 2022;57(5):1108-1120.
Orphanet: Interstitial lung disease specific to childhood. ORPHA:264656.
Fan LL, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Childhood Interstitial Lung Disease. Pediatr Clin North Am. 2021;68(4):789-807.
